content.title: What is a String?
content.description: A String is a sequence of characters stored together to represent text. Strings are one of the most commonly used data types in programming.

content.content: Strings are everywhere in software development. Usernames, passwords, search queries, emails, URLs, and messages are all examples of string data. Understanding how strings work is essential for solving real-world problems and coding interview questions.

content.title: Did You Know?
content.content: Search engines, chat applications, spell checkers, and text editors rely heavily on string manipulation algorithms.

content.title: String Representation
steps: Chars: H E L L O

content.content: String Characteristics

A string is essentially an array of characters. Each character can be accessed using its index. Most programming languages store strings as sequences of characters that can be traversed and manipulated efficiently.

content.title: Indexing
content.description: String indexing usually starts from 0. The first character is at index 0 and the last character is at index length - 1.

content.content: Common String Operations
String manipulation involves performing various operations on text data. These operations form the foundation of many algorithms and applications.

items.question: Traversal
items.answer: Visit every character one by one.

items.question: Concatenation
items.answer: Combine two or more strings together.

items.question: Substring
items.answer: Extract a portion of a string.

items.question: Searching
items.answer: Find a character or pattern inside a string.

items.question: Replacement
items.answer: Replace characters or words with new values.

content.content: String Traversal
Traversal means visiting every character in the string one by one. This is commonly used for counting characters, searching patterns, and performing transformations.
String Concatenation
Concatenation means joining two or more strings together to create a new string.

content.title: Performance Tip
content.content: Repeated string concatenation can be expensive. Many languages provide StringBuilder or similar utilities for efficient modifications.
Substring Extraction
A substring is a smaller portion extracted from a larger string using starting and ending positions.
String Searching
Searching involves finding a character, word, or pattern inside a string. This operation is fundamental in text processing applications.

content.title: Real-World Usage
content.description: Search engines, autocomplete systems, and document editors perform millions of string searches every day.

content.content: String Reversal
String reversal is a popular interview problem where characters are rearranged in reverse order.
String Comparison
String comparison determines whether two strings are equal or which string comes first lexicographically.

items.answer: Reverse characters efficiently using Two Pointers.

items.question: Check Palindrome
items.answer: Determine whether a string reads the same forward and backward.

content.title: Real-Life Analogy
content.content: Think of a string as a word written on individual tiles arranged in a row. String manipulation is similar to rearranging, replacing, or inspecting those tiles to create new words or patterns.

content.title: Industry Usage
content.content: String processing is essential in search engines, chatbots, compilers, cybersecurity systems, text editors, and natural language processing.
Common Mistakes

items.question: What is the most common beginner mistake?
items.answer: Accessing characters outside valid string indices.

items.question: Why do string operations become slow?
items.answer: Repeated concatenations create new string objects.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Many advanced string problems can be solved using HashMaps, Sliding Window, Two Pointers, Prefix Arrays, and Pattern Matching algorithms.
